_meta.purpose: Khajistan TV programming — show catalogue, weekly grid, dated month.
_meta.clock: One station clock: Pakistan Standard Time, UTC+5, no daylight saving. The stream runs continuously; a slot names the hour a show starts, and a set tuning in joins whatever is on wherever it has got to.

channels.name: Channel 1
channels.line: Ripped media. VHS, DVD and film, transferred here and played as it came off the carrier — features, film song, television drama, trailers, weddings.

channels.name: Channel 2
channels.line: Ripped audio. Tape, disc and vinyl, with no picture — the Lost Lollywood Soundtracks and the records off our own shelf.

mondo-bizarro.name: Mondo Bizarro
mondo-bizarro.line: Omar Ali Khan's own show. Lollywood club, desi funk, Dracula in Pakistan, the pakoras.

saturday-street.name: Saturday Street
saturday-street.line: Christmas in Garhi Shahu. Whatever the street was playing.

strange-archive.name: Strange Archive
strange-archive.line: Juntar muntar, parts of body, and the records on no other shelf.

hi-tea.name: Hi Tea
hi-tea.line: The afternoon record. Mummy daddy, daddy ka shukriya.

prime-signal.name: Prime Signal
prime-signal.line: The PIA mix. The airline had its own orchestra.

archive-program.name: Archive Program
archive-program.line: Khorasan, Mashriq–Maghreb, Shabbat, Ramzan. Four mixes, a region each.

lollywood-soundtracks.name: Lost Lollywood Soundtracks
lollywood-soundtracks.line: The music of 498 Pakistani films, cut from Khajistan's own rips by Yaseen Hameed over two years in Hyderabad, Sindh. Whole soundtracks, end to end.

mehfil-3.name: Mehfil
mehfil-3.line: The evening concert with no picture. A sitting-room recording, a stage night.

kabul-and-herat-3.name: Kabul & Herat
kabul-and-herat-3.line: Afghan song in Dari and Pashto, off the record. Ghazal, tappa, the wedding band.

baghdad-3.name: Baghdad
baghdad-3.line: Iraqi and Levantine song without a picture — the mawal, the choubi.

punjab-side-3.name: Punjab Side
punjab-side-3.line: Punjabi and Saraiki folk as the cassette labels cut it. Dohra, mahiya, vol. 17 of somebody's best.

vinyl-rips.name: Vinyl Rips
vinyl-rips.line: Pakistani film soundtracks off the 45s, EPs and LPs, with the EMI catalogue number still on the label. Sound only.

the-break.name: The Break
the-break.line: Video-company logos, cassette-label stings, the odd cigarette advert. Between programmes.

jordan-television.name: Jordan Television
jordan-television.line: The Jordanian state channel's own evenings, mostly from the 1990s.

someones-wedding.name: Someone's Wedding
someones-wedding.line: Baraats, mehndis, birthdays, the family camcorder. Nobody made these to be broadcast.

coming-attractions.name: Coming Attractions
coming-attractions.line: Trailers, run as a reel. The Filmfarsi volumes and the Hi-Tech Films promos.

ptv.name: PTV
ptv.line: The state broadcaster's drama, off DVD transfers, in disc-and-part order.

filmfarsi.name: Filmfarsi
filmfarsi.line: Pre-revolution Iranian cinema and the colour restorations.

the-feature.name: The Feature
the-feature.line: The full picture. Lollywood, Pashto cinema, whatever the print we hold will carry.

mehfil-on-tape.name: Mehfil on Tape
mehfil-on-tape.line: The evening concert as somebody's cassette caught it. A sitting-room mehfil, a stage night.

the-voice.name: The Voice
the-voice.line: The woman's voice carrying the popular song, from Lahore to Kabul.

lollywood.name: Lollywood
lollywood.line: The song sequence pulled out of the film.

tape-feature.name: The Tape Feature
tape-feature.line: The film as it reached a living room. A rental cassette, end to end, tracking as it was.

tape-transfers.name: Tape Transfers
tape-transfers.line: The rest of the shelf, played through as it was transferred. Song compilations, an evening of PTV taped off the air, whatever was on the cassette.

khajistan-filmfarsi-trailers-reel-1.title: Filmfarsi Trailers — Vol. 1
khajistan-filmfarsi-trailers-reel-1.description: A feature-length procession of Iranian coming attractions built around the voices, faces and promises of popular cinema. The reel includes Ganj-e Qarun (1965), Siamak Yasami’s landmark box-office melodrama, among a much larger field of trailers preserved in their original sequence. Identified passages include Kaka Siah (1973).

filmfarsi-trailers-vol-10.title: Filmfarsi Trailers — Vol. 10
filmfarsi-trailers-vol-10.description: A trailer reel that runs on into a cabaret programme — the tape carries both and they are kept together, because the join is how this material survived. Individual passages are not yet identified.

khajistan-filmfarsi-trailers-reel-2.title: Filmfarsi Trailers — Vol. 2
khajistan-filmfarsi-trailers-reel-2.description: A compact hour of Iranian trailers in which fantasy, comedy, romance and social aspiration arrive one after another. Ali Hatami’s Hasan Kachal (1969), the celebrated filmmaker’s first feature, anchors a reel crowded with further attractions. Identified passages include Kaj Kolah Khan (1973).

filmfarsi-trailers-vol-9.title: Filmfarsi Trailers — Vol. 9
filmfarsi-trailers-vol-9.description: Seventy-four minutes of Iranian coming attractions off a single reel. Identified passages include Sad Kilo Damad (1961). The rest is not yet named title by title; the reel is presented whole, as it was cut.
